## What is a Regression Model?

Given $n$ observations $(\mathbf{x}_i, y_i)$, $i = 1, \ldots, n$,
classical regression focuses on relating the conditional mean
of the response to the covariates:

$$
E(Y_i \mid \mathbf{x}_i) = h^{-1}\{\eta(\mathbf{x}_i)\}.
$$

Much statistical research has focused on flexibility in the predictor
$\eta(\mathbf{x}_i)$:

- nonlinear and additive effects,
- random effects and hierarchical structures,
- spatial and spatiotemporal effects.

\medskip

The conditional mean is only **one** feature of the conditional
response distribution.


## Regression Beyond the Mean

**Classic linear model**:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}

$$Y_i\mid x_i \sim N(\mu_i, \sigma^2),$$
$$\mu_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1x_i.$$

\medskip

- Linear conditional mean.
- Constant conditional variance.

:::
::: {.column width="56%"}

\medskip

```{r}
#| label: plot-intro-linear
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| echo: false
#| results: hide

set.seed(6020)
d <- data.frame("x" = runif(1000, -3, 3))
d$y <- 0.6 * d$x^2 + rnorm(nrow(d), sd = exp(0.5 * d$x))

m <- gamlss2(y ~ x, data = d)

nd <- data.frame("x" = seq(min(d$x), max(d$x), length = 300))

plot_fit <- function(model) {
  pd <- predict(model, newdata = nd)

  f <- quantile(pd, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))

  plot(y ~ x, data = d, pch = 16, col = adjustcolor(1, 0.2))
  matlines(nd$x, f, col = c(4, 2, 4), lty = 1, lwd = 3)
  legend("topleft",
    c("Fitted mean", "5th / 95th centiles"),
    col = c(2, 4), lty = 1, lwd = 3, bty = "n")
}

plot_fit(m)
```

:::
::::


## Regression Beyond the Mean

**Nonlinear (additive) model**:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}

$$\mu_i = \beta_0 + f(x_i),$$
$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_i\mid x_i) = \sigma^2.$$

\medskip

- Nonlinear conditional mean.
- Constant conditional variance.
- Intervals retain constant width.
- Nonlinearity and changing dispersion are separate modeling decisions.

:::
::: {.column width="56%"}

\medskip

```{r}
#| label: plot-intro-nonlinear
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| echo: false
#| results: hide

m <- gamlss2(y ~ s(x), data = d)
plot_fit(m)
```

:::
::::


## Regression Beyond the Mean

**Model location and scale together**:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}

$$\mu_i = \beta_{0\mu} + f_\mu(x_i),$$
$$\log(\sigma_i) = \beta_{0\sigma} + f_\sigma(x_i).$$

- Here, $\sigma$ is the standard deviation.
- Changes the width of the conditional distribution.

:::
::: {.column width="56%"}

\medskip

```{r}
#| label: plot-intro-locscale
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| echo: false
#| results: hide

m <- gamlss2(y ~ s(x) | s(x), data = d)
plot_fit(m)
```

:::
::::


## Scientific Targets Beyond the Mean

For a response $Y$ and covariates $\mathbf{x}$, scientific interest may concern:

- conditional reference limits: $Q_{0.025}(\mathbf{x})$ and $Q_{0.975}(\mathbf{x)}$,
- relative or absolute variability\newline
  (e.g., standard deviation or coefficient of variation),
- asymmetry and tail behavior,
- threshold events: $P(Y > c \mid \mathbf{x})$,
- a predictive distribution for a future observation.

\medskip

Each target is a function of the conditional distribution. Distribution choice and
parameter predictors determine which changes the model can represent.


## Equal Means, Different Tail Probabilities

```{r}
#| label: plot-same-mean
#| echo: false
#| out-width: "90%"
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-align: center

y <- seq(-2, 23, length.out = 900)

mu <- 10
sigma <- c(2, 4)
threshold <- 15

cols <- c("#2F5F9E", "#FB9E19")
ltys <- c(1, 2)

d <- sapply(sigma, function(s) dnorm(y, mu, s))
p <- pnorm(threshold, mu, sigma, lower.tail = FALSE)

par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

matplot(y, d, type = "n",
  xlab = "Response", ylab = "Density",
  ylim = c(0, 0.22))

for(j in 2:1) {
  polygon(c(y, rev(y)),
    c(d[, j], rep(0, length(y))),
    col = adjustcolor(cols[j], alpha.f = 0.2),
    border = NA)
}

yt <- seq(threshold, max(y), length.out = 500)

for(j in 2:1) {
  polygon(c(yt, rev(yt)),
    c(dnorm(yt, mu, sigma[j]), rep(0, length(yt))),
    col = adjustcolor(cols[j], alpha.f = 0.45),
    border = NA)
}

abline(v = threshold, lty = 3, lwd = 1.5, col = "gray50")

matlines(y, d, col = cols, lty = ltys, lwd = 3)
i <- y >= 15
matlines(y[i], d[i, ], col = cols, lty = 1, lwd = 3)

axis(3, at = threshold, labels = "Threshold",
  tick = FALSE, line = -0.5, col.axis = "gray40")

legend("topright",
  sprintf("SD %g: P(Y > %g) = %.2f%%", sigma, threshold, 100 * p),
  col = cols, lty = 1, lwd = 3, bty = "n")
```

- Both distributions have mean 10,
- but their probabilities of exceeding 15 differ by a factor of `r round(p[2] / p[1])`.


## Model Specification

Any parameter of a population distribution $\mathbf{\mathcal{D}}$ may be modeled by explanatory
variables
$$
\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathbf{\mathcal{D}}\left(\theta_{1}(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\beta}_{1}), \,\, \dots \, , \,\,
  \theta_{K}(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\beta}_{K})\right),
$$

```{r}
#| label: plot-example-distributions
#| out-width: "80%"
#| fig-height: 1.5
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-align: center
#| echo: false
#| results: hide

mypoly <- function() {
  p <- cbind(c(x, rev(x)), c(y, rep(0, length(y))))
  polygon(p, border = NA, col = "#FB9E19")
  lines(y ~ x, lwd = 8)
}
x <- seq(0, 10, length = 200)

par(mar = rep(0, 4), mfrow = c(1, 4))
plot((y <- dnorm(x, mean = 5)) ~ x, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
  lwd = 6)
mypoly()
plot((y <- dgamma(x, shape = 3, rate = 1.2)) ~ x, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
  lwd = 6)
mypoly()
x <- seq(0, 0.99, length = 200)
plot((y <- gamlss.dist::dBEZI(x, mu = 0.4, sigma = 6, nu = 0.6)) ~ x, type = "l", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
  lwd = 6)
mypoly()
#plot((y <- gamlss.dist::dBCPE(x, mu = 5, sigma = 0.3, nu = 0, tau = 7)) ~ x, type = "l", axes = FALSE,
#  xlab = "", ylab = "", lwd = 6)
#mypoly()
x <- seq(1.5, 10.3, length = 200)
plot((y <- gamlss.dist::dBCPE(x, mu = 5, sigma = 0.3, nu = 0.01, tau = 14)) ~ x, type = "l", axes = FALSE,
  xlab = "", ylab = "", lwd = 6)
mypoly()
```
with $\boldsymbol{\beta} = (\boldsymbol{\beta}_1^\top, \ldots, \boldsymbol{\beta}_K^\top)^\top$.

\bigskip

Each parameter is linked to a structured additive predictor
$$
h_{k}(\theta_{k}(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\beta}_k)) =
  f_{1k}(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\beta}_{1k}) + \ldots + f_{J_kk}(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\beta}_{J_kk}),
$$

- $j = 1, \dots, J_k$ and $k = 1, \dots, K$.
- $h_k( \cdot )$: Link functions for each distribution parameter.
- $f_{jk}( \cdot )$: Model terms of one or more variables.


## Model Terms $f_{jk}( \cdot )$

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="28%"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-nonlinear
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"

par(mar = c(4.1, 4.1, 4.1, 1.1))
set.seed(333)
n <- 100
f <- bamlss:::simfun("double")
idata <- data.frame("z" = seq(0, 1, length = n))
idata$y <- bamlss::scale2(with(idata, 0.6 + f(z) + rnorm(n, sd = 1)), 0, 1)
ib <- gamlss2(y ~ s(z, bs = "ps"), data = idata)
plot(ib, ylab = "f(x)", xlab = "x",
  main = "Nonlinear Effects")
```

:::

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-surfaces
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"

par(mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 4.1, 0.1))
z <- 2 * volcano
x <- 10 * (1:nrow(z))
y <- 10 * (1:ncol(z))
xy <- expand.grid(x, y)
xy$z <- as.numeric(z)
bamlss::plot3d(xy, type = "mba", symmetric = FALSE, xlab = "x1", ylab = "x2", zlab = "f(x1, x2)",
  main = "Two-Dimensional Surfaces")
```

::: {.column width="21%"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-lasso
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"

text2 <- function(x, y = NULL, ...) {
  if(is.null(y))
    y <- x
  xy <- par("usr")
  xr <- range(xy[1:2])
  yr <- range(xy[3:4])
  x <- xy[1] + x * diff(xr)
  y <- xy[3] + y * diff(yr)
  text(x, y, ...)
}

if(!file.exists("lasso.rda")) {
  ## Simulated fusion Lasso example.
  bmu <- c(0,0,0,0.5,0.5,0.5,1,1,1)
  bsigma <- c(0,0,0,-0.7,-0.7,0,0,0.5,0.5)
  id <- factor(sort(rep(1:length(bmu), length.out = 300)))
     
  ## Response.
  set.seed(111)
  y <- bmu[id] + rnorm(length(id), sd = exp(-1 + bsigma[id]))

  f <- y ~ la(id,type=3) | la(id,type=3)

  b1 <- gamlss2(f)

  save(b1, file = "lasso.rda")
} else {
  load("lasso.rda")
}
par(mar = c(4.1, 4.3, 4.1, 6.1))
plot_lasso(b1, which = "coefficients", terms = 1, main = FALSE, zoom = c(7, 5), lwd = 2)
mtext("LASSO & Factor Clustering", side = 3, line = 1.5, cex = 1.2, font = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-spatial
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-format: png
#| fig-dpi: 200
#| out-width: "100%"

par(mar = c(2.1, 0.1, 4.1, 0.1))
library("spdep")
library("sp")
m <- readRDS("data/gadm36_AUT_3_sp.rds")
co <- coordinates(m)
m@data$lon <- co[, 1]
m@data$lat <- co[, 2]
## m <- subset(m, lon > -10 & lat > 35.7)

set.seed(123)
m@data$y <- sin(bamlss::scale2(co[, 1], -3, 3)) + cos(bamlss::scale2(co[, 2], -3, 3)) + rnorm(nrow(co), sd = 0.3)
bamlss::plotmap(m, select = "y", color = colorspace::diverge_hcl, legend = FALSE, lwd = 0.1,
  main = "Spatially Correlated Effects f(x) = f(s)")
m0 <- readRDS("data/gadm36_AUT_0_sp.rds")
plot(m0, add = TRUE, lwd = 1)
plot(readRDS("data/gadm36_AUT_2_sp.rds"), add = TRUE, lwd = 0.5)
```

::: {.column width="29%"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-random
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"

par(mar = c(4.1, 4.1, 4.1, 0.1))
set.seed(111)
id <- factor(rep(1:8, length = 100))
m <- rnorm(8, sd = 0.6)
y <- m[id] + rnorm(length(id), sd = 0.6)
b <- gamlss2(y ~ s(id, bs = "re"))
plot(b, ylab = "f(id)", xlab = "id", spar = FALSE)
mtext("Random Intercepts f(x) = f(id)", side = 3, line = 1.5, cex = 1.2, font = 2)
```

::: {.column width="23%"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-effects-neural
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| out-width: "100%"

par(mar = c(0.1, 1.1, 3.6, 0.1))
plot_jpeg = function(path, add=FALSE)
{
  require('jpeg')
  jpg = readJPEG(path, native=T) # read the file
  res = dim(jpg)[2:1] # get the resolution, [x, y]
  if (!add) # initialize an empty plot area if add==FALSE
    plot(1,1,xlim=c(1,res[1]),ylim=c(1,res[2]),asp=1,type='n',xaxs='i',yaxs='i',xaxt='n',yaxt='n',xlab='',ylab='',bty='n')
  rasterImage(jpg,1,1,res[1],res[2])
}
plot_jpeg('figures/nnet.jpg') 
mtext("Neural Networks", side = 3, line = 1, cex = 1.2, font = 2)
```
